AeroChu Team Report (built & used by @slucin03 )

Today, I am featuring a very strong Raichu team, piloted by Juan Lucin for a 2nd place finish at the latest VR tournament. It has very huge damage output while keeping solid bulk across the board.

Team: 

Raichu: 
Raichu has been popping off lately, making it at least a Top 5 Mega Pokémon in the current metagame. It's incredible speed tier paired with the crazy damage output is very dangerous for many teams. There are still some teams out there that have no electric resist, making Raichu even more powerful. Focus Blast is a good move to threaten Kingambit and deal some decent damage into Incineroar or Garchomp. Meanwhile, Fake Out can allow Kingambit to setup a Swords Dance or it can be used to reposition yourself nicely. While the spread looks like, it comes straight out of the recruitment screen, it is quite smart. Opposing Raichu is a nuisance for the team, so I figured that it is nice to outspeed it. Another cool tech is that you outspeed many Sylveon in Tailwind (they are around 95 speed) which allows you to Zap Cannon them before and follow up with a Wave Crash / Hyper Voice on your own. The bulk is also incredible. Surviving Life Orb Sucker Punch from Kingambit seemed very important to me (32+ Atk Life Orb Kingambit Sucker Punch vs. 32 HP / 1 Def Mega Raichu Y: 140-165 (83.8 - 98.8%) -- guaranteed 2HKO). The one Special Defense point allows you to survive Earth Power from Life Orb Venusaur (32+ SpA Life Orb Venusaur Earth Power vs. 32 HP / 1 SpD Mega Raichu Y: 146-174 (87.4 - 104.1%) -- 18.75% chance to OHKO) better [31.75% chance otherwise] as well as Helping Hand Hyper Voice from Sylveon under Trick Room conditions for example (30+ SpA Fairy Feather Pixilate Sylveon Helping Hand Hyper Voice vs. 32 HP / 1 SpD Mega Raichu Y: 142-168 (85 - 100.5%) -- 6.25% chance to OHKO).

Sylveon: 
One of the best partners next to Raichu is Sylveon. It appreciates the para support a ton and is able to threaten Garchomp, one of the most annoying Pokémon for Raichu. The moveset is incredibly strong. And yes, Detect is better if you run into Imprison + Protect stuff. The spread is pretty unusual though. Many Sylveon either opt for more bulk to survive Dire Claw from Sneasler or more Special Attack to get the knockout on Kingambit with Hyper Beam for example. The Sylveon usually run around 95 speed, just enough to outrun paralyzed Froslass / Sneasler. I went for 103 speed instead. Getting the jump on opposing Sylveon is nice obviously but you are also able to outrun some Basculegion (very slow ones such as the one on the ScovLass team usually) or Max Speed (Adamant) Kingambit. That way you can take games by surprise. I also really liked outspeeding Delphox & opposing Raichu in Tailwind. We still got enough bulk to withstand a Wave Crash from Choice Scarf Basculegion (32 Atk Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash vs. 11 HP / 12 Def Sylveon: 154-182 (85 - 100.5%) -- 6.25% chance to OHKO) or Sludge Bomb from Venusaur (32+ SpA Life Orb Venusaur Sludge Bomb vs. 11 HP / 0 SpD Sylveon: 151-179 (83.4 - 98.8%) -- guaranteed 2HKO).

Kingambit: 
Another great Pokémon to take advanatge from Raichu's toolkit is Kingambit. I already explained that you can set a Swords Dance up due to Fake Out pressure but the paralysis is what pushes Swords Dance Kingambit to the next level. Being able to outspeed paralyzed (Modest) Floette or just Incineroar, it is all very beneficial. I decided to go with 79 speed to also outrun the 90 base Pokémon (Paralyzed or in Tailwind) such as Annihilape or Arcanine-Hisui. The one def point is also pretty important. It heavily increases the chance to survive Life Orb Earthquake + Rough Skin + Life Orb recoil, giving you an extra turn to attack (32 Atk Life Orb Garchomp Earthquake vs. 24 HP / 1 Def Kingambit: 140-166 (70.3 - 83.4%) -- 43.75% chance to OHKO) [otherwise 62.5% chance]. You are also always able to survive Wave Crash from Life Orb Basculegion + your own Life Orb recoil (32+ Atk Life Orb Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash vs. 24 HP / 1 Def Kingambit: 151-179 (75.8 - 89.9%) -- guaranteed 2HKO). Running max attack is important to secure some knockouts with +2 Sucker Punch on Charizard or Garchomp.

Sneasler: 
The best friend of Kingambit? Sneasler! It threatens all Pokémon that resist your dark Moves (Fairies & Dark Types). It also gives you a second Fake Out option which makes it even harder for your opponent to Protect in front of it. That is because you threaten the switch into your second Fake Out user and if your opponent clicked Protect that turn, they are vulnerable the following turn. Poison Touch Sneasler is quite nasty, spreading poisons everywhere. Jolly Nature is the better option cause you need to outspeed Whimsicott and it's also another bonus to outrun all the 110s (Maushold, Staraptor, Metagross, Xchu).

Basculegion: 
Basculegion pairs super well with the other physical attackers, threatening Delphox and being a great pick into Sand teams which your two megas can struggle against. Surviving Sucker Punch from non damage boosting Kingambit is more important than ever which is what the 11 Defense are for (32+ Atk Kingambit Sucker Punch vs. 0 HP / 11 Def Basculegion: 168-200 (86.1 - 102.5%) -- 12.5% chance to OHKO). I did not want to drop too much Attack to still get the knockout on Careful Incineroar (-1 28+ Atk Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion Wave Crash vs. 32 HP / 14 Def Incineroar: 204-244 (100.9 - 120.7%) -- guaranteed OHKO). The speed stat might seem random but outspeeding Adamant M-Tyranitar was on my checklist and since it hits 123, I just made the Basculegion two points faster than that, catching some opposing Basculegion or Charizard as well.

Aerodactyl: 
I love M-Aerodactyl. I am very happy that it found it's place on a non Charizard team. I am quite aware that Raichu and Aerodactyl speedtie if you bring both of them and decide to Mega evolve your Raichu but I just could not ignore opposing M-Aerodactyl when creating the spread. We should talk first about its moves though. While Garchomp can be fairly annoying and you can make a case for Ice Fang, I am a big believer of Protect, making it harder for your opponent to get the knockout quickly on your Aerodactyl. The STAB moves should not be dropped since, Dual Wingbeat is just too important for Venusaur alone and Rock Slide is...well it's Rock Slide :] 12 Attack ensures a clean OHKO on Sneasler (12 Atk Aerodactyl Dual Wingbeat (2 hits) vs. 0 HP / 2 Def Sneasler: 156-184 (100.6 - 118.7%) -- guaranteed OHKO). Funnily enough, the damage from -1 Mega Dual Wingbeat is the same, so you also get the knockout in that scenario. There are some games you want to bring regular Aerodactyl next to your Mega-Raichu which is why I made the bulk based on some regular Aero calcs as well. You can take an Aqua Jet from Mystic Water Basculegion for example (32+ Atk Mystic Water Adaptability Basculegion Aqua Jet vs. 18 HP / 4 Def Aerodactyl: 148-176 (85.5 - 101.7%) -- 6.25% chance to OHKO). Being able to take a Close Combat from Sneasler is also very beneficial.

Matchups: 
vs Big Six - One of the matchups where you can bring regular Aerodactyl and Mega-Raichu. Basculegion is a very important piece here. Try to use it to trade effectively. Alternatively, Swords Dance Kingambit is strong but you need to be wary of Floette & opposing Low Kick Kingambit which is why it's hard to execute. All Pokémon can be brought (I won with Aero + Basc, Raichu Sylv back but I also won with Sneasler + Gambit, Raichu Basc back)

vs Setup Balance - Non Blastoise versions struggle a lot into Aerodactyl + Basculegion + Sylveon. Sylveon removes Kingambit while Aerodactyl covers for Sneasler. Use Basculegion for their mega (Delphox, Floette). Raichu is not a bad pick either due to outspeeding Sneasler but it makes you matchup into Sinistcha quite awkward.

vs ZardVenu - It heavily depends on the comp. Against many, you can bring regular Aerodactyl and Mega-Raichu. Raichu is able to threaten Toxapex which is otherwise slightly annoying to deal with. Use Swords Dance Kingambit as well to take huge knockouts in the early game.

vs RaichuRaptor - Raichu mirrors are always annoying to play. With your Raichu most likely being faster, you got the advantage however. Use Sylveon and Raichu to break holes with Kingambit in the back to counter their Trick Room. I don't recommend bringing Aerodactyl, go with Basculegion instead.

Conclusion: 
A team where you can bring all your Pokémon in many matchups has to be good. I am not entirely sure if the team will see much use at Worlds but you should play with it and see if you like it.
General advice: Don't get frustrated if you lose games early on. Understanding a team takes time and requires some practice first. Don't toss it immediately, just because the first games don't go your way. Use it as learning experience and improve that way!
